gbm_population_evidence.quote: Histologically confirmed high-grade glioma, with standard radiotherapy and chemotherapy post-surgical resection deemed unsuccessful, and recurrence confirmed by imaging.

candidate_evidence.quote: Specific Mode Electroacupuncture Stimulation (SMES) can open the blood-brain barrier, enhancing the concentration of albumin-bound paclitaxel (ABX) in tumor tissues

role_evidence.quote: ABX was administered intravenously at a dose of 110mg/m2 on days 1 and 8 of a 28-day treatment cycle

agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: exhibits antitumor effects in vitro that are 1400 times stronger than those of temozolomide

role_evidence.quote: Temozolomide（TMZ） was given orally or intravenously 150mg/(m2·d) for 5 days, repeated every 28 days for 6 cycles

coder_notes: Population is 'high-grade glioma' with glioblastoma not named, so the trial fails S5 (high_grade_glioma_unspecified). Paclitaxel (albumin-bound) has its own stated antitumour hypothesis and is paired with electroacupuncture (SMES, a device) to open the BBB, so it is a candidate with device_dependent true; the SMES device is not listed as an agent. Both arms are registered as type OTHER; the 'TMZ group' works as the standard-of-care control arm. The brief summary says SMES enhances ABX concentration in tumour tissue, but no tumour PK or pharmacodynamic measurement is listed among the outcomes, so both are coded no.
